findings.title: argon2i_32 does not enforce the minimum Argon2 block count, causing a heap buffer overflow
findings.evidence: argon2i_32 copies the caller-supplied nb_blocks straight into config.nb_blocks (line 328) and sizes the work area as malloc(nb_blocks * 1024) (line 345) with no lower-bound validation, even though monocypher.h documents nb_blocks >= 8 * nb_lanes (monocypher.h:160) and this binding hard-codes nb_lanes = 1 (line 330). Inside monocypher.c crypto_argon2 the effective block count is rounded down (segment_size = nb_blocks/nb_lanes/4, lane_size = segment_size*4, monocypher.c:752-754), but before that it unconditionally fills the first two 1024-byte blocks of every lane (monocypher.c:776-782), i.e. it always writes 2048 bytes to blocks[0] and blocks[1]. With nb_blocks = 1, segment_size and lane_size are 0, so the buffer is only 1024 bytes and the write at monocypher.c:781 overruns the heap allocation by 1024 bytes (nb_blocks = 0 is worse: malloc(0) followed by a 2048-byte write). With nb_blocks in 0..3 lane_size is 0, so last_block = blocks - 1 and the read at monocypher.c:911 also reads 1024 bytes before the buffer. Reachable directly from Python, e.g. monocypher.argon2i_32(1, 1, b'pw', b'salt1'), so any application that forwards an untrusted block count into this binding suffers heap memory corruption.
